title: Yale Digital Ethics Center Symposium (DECS) 2026 in USA | Fully Funded Opportunity for PhD Students and Postdoctoral Scholars
summary: The Yale Digital Ethics Center (DEC) is inviting applications for the inaugural Digital Ethics Center Symposium (DECS) 2026, a prestigious international event designed to showcase the work of emerging scholars examining the ethical, legal, social, and governance implications of digital technologies. Taking place on October 16, 2026, at Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, the symposium offers PhD students and postdoctoral researchers a unique platform to present their work, engage with leading scholars, and contribute to critical discussions shaping the future of digital governance and ethics. Selected participants will receive fully funded travel support, accommodation, recognition through the inaugural DECS Best Paper Award, and opportunities for future collaboration with Yale’s Digital Ethics Center. About the Digital Ethics Center Symposium (DECS) The Digital Ethics Center Symposium is a new international academic forum established by Yale University s Digital Ethics Center to support early-career researchers whose work explores the ethical and human dimensions of digital transformation. The symposium focuses on the Governance, Ethical, Legal, and Social Implications (GELSI) of digital technologies and seeks to foster meaningful dialogue between emerging scholars and established experts in the field. Participants will present peer-reviewed papers and receive detailed commentary from Digital Ethics Center researchers, followed by scholarly discussion and feedback. Symposium Theme DECS 2026 welcomes research that examines the governance and societal implications of digital technologies, including topics related to: • Digital ethics • Artificial intelligence governance • Technology policy • Data ethics • Privacy and surveillance • Algorithmic accountability • Responsible innovation • Human-centered technology • Digital rights and regulation • Ethical dimensions of emerging technologies The symposium particularly encourages work that can inform policy development and governance frameworks across different jurisdictions. Benefits of Participation Selected presenters will receive: • Full round-trip travel support to New Haven, Connecticut • Two nights of accommodation • The inaugural DECS Best Paper Award medal • An invitation to collaborate with Professor Luciano Floridi and Digital Ethics Center researchers during the Spring 2027 semester • Opportunities to receive feedback from leading scholars in digital ethics • International academic visibility and networking opportunities Publication Opportunity One of the most attractive features of the symposium is the publication opportunity available to applicants. All high-quality submissions including papers not selected for presentation will be considered for publication in a special issue of Philosophy Technology , a leading journal in the field. This provides an exceptional opportunity for early-career researchers to gain scholarly recognition and contribute to ongoing debates in digital ethics and technology governance. Who Can Apply? Applications are open to: • PhD students • Postdoctoral scholars Applicants from all countries are encouraged to apply. The symposium is specifically designed to support emerging researchers whose work explores the ethical and societal dimensions of digital technologies. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must ensure that: • Their submission is original work. • The paper is not formally published. • The manuscript is not currently under review elsewhere. • The manuscript is not committed for publication with another outlet. • Preprints and working papers may be submitted. • Any publicly available preprint version must be disclosed in the application. • Only one submission may be made as first author. Applicants may appear as co-authors on additional submissions. Application Requirements Applicants must submit: 1. Short Curriculum Vitae A CV of no more than two pages highlighting relevant academic and research experience. File format: LastName-FirstName-DECS.CV.pdf 2. Paper Abstract An abstract of up to 2,000 words describing the paper to be presented. File format: LastName-FirstName-DECS.Abstract.pdf Application Process Applicants should submit their complete application package via email. Applications must be sent to: 📧 [dec@yale.edu](mailto:dec@yale.edu) Why You Should Apply The Yale Digital Ethics Center Symposium offers more than a conference presentation opportunity. It provides emerging scholars with access to a global network of researchers, direct engagement with one of the world s leading digital ethics centers, opportunities for publication, and the chance to influence conversations surrounding the governance of digital technologies. For researchers interested in artificial intelligence, digital governance, ethics, law, and technology policy, DECS 2026 represents a valuable platform to showcase innovative ideas and contribute to shaping the future of responsible digital transformation. Conclusion The Yale Digital Ethics Center Symposium (DECS) 2026 is an outstanding opportunity for PhD students and postdoctoral scholars working on digital ethics and technology governance. With fully funded travel, accommodation, publication opportunities, scholarly feedback, and collaboration prospects with leading experts, the symposium provides a powerful platform for advancing research and professional development. If your work explores the ethical, legal, social, or governance dimensions of digital technologies, be sure to submit your application before August 30, 2026 . Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage . title: Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026: Fully Remote Global Research Fellowship for Professionals Transitioning into AI Governance
summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping industries, governments, and societies worldwide. As AI systems become increasingly powerful, the need for skilled professionals capable of developing effective governance frameworks, safety policies, and risk mitigation strategies has never been greater. To help address this growing global challenge, Arcadia Impact has opened applications for its AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026 Cohort , a prestigious research programme designed for experienced professionals who want to transition into frontier AI governance. This highly selective programme offers participants an opportunity to conduct policy-relevant AI governance research alongside internationally recognized experts while maintaining their current professional commitments. Running over 12 weeks on a part-time basis, the programme is fully remote and welcomes applicants from around the world. Although voluntary and unpaid, the fellowship provides invaluable exposure, professional networking opportunities, practical research experience, and a proven pathway into careers focused on AI governance, AI safety, and policy development. About the Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce The AI Governance Taskforce is a specialized research programme that supports experienced professionals seeking to transition into careers focused on reducing catastrophic and systemic risks associated with transformative artificial intelligence. Unlike many AI education programmes that focus on technical development or AI ethics generally, the AI Governance Taskforce specifically concentrates on frontier AI governance . Participants work on policy-focused research designed to improve governance systems capable of addressing advanced AI risks before they become major global threats. The programme enables professionals from diverse disciplines to apply their existing expertise to one of the world s fastest-growing policy areas while receiving mentorship from leaders in AI governance and safety. Why This Programme Matters As governments, international organizations, and technology companies race to regulate increasingly advanced AI systems, there is a significant global shortage of professionals who understand both public policy and frontier AI governance. Arcadia Impact created the AI Governance Taskforce to bridge this gap by providing professionals with: Practical research experience Exposure to real-world AI governance challenges High-level mentorship Collaborative policy development experience Professional networks within the AI safety community Participants leave the programme with stronger credentials that position them for future opportunities in AI governance, research, public policy, and international organizations. Programme Overview The Autumn 2026 cohort has been carefully structured to accommodate working professionals. Programme Details Programme Duration: 12 weeks Programme Dates: 12 October 2026 – 15 January 2027 Year-End Break: Two-week holiday break between 18 December 2026 and 4 January 2027 Commitment: Approximately 8 hours per week Delivery Mode: Fully remote Location: Global Programme Type: Voluntary and unpaid Available Positions: Approximately 20 Research Associate places Participants can continue with their existing careers while contributing to meaningful AI governance research. What Participants Will Do Research Associates become members of multidisciplinary research teams composed of four individuals. Each team works closely with: A dedicated Research Team Leader A leading AI governance expert Other experienced professionals from diverse disciplines Together, they investigate pressing AI governance questions and produce policy-oriented research intended to influence real-world decision-making. Typical research outputs include: Academic-style preprint papers Policy briefs Government policy memoranda Research articles Stakeholder reports These publications are designed to address challenges surrounding advanced AI governance and catastrophic AI risks. Learn from World-Leading AI Governance Experts Participants receive direct guidance from senior practitioners working across some of the world s most respected AI safety and governance organizations. Expert partners have included professionals affiliated with: UK AI Security Institute (AISI) Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI) AI Incident Database (AIID) MIT AI Risk Initiative (AIRI) Centre for Long-Term Resilience (CLTR) SaferAI The Future Society Future of Life Institute (FLI) Leading universities and academic institutions Research Team Leaders work alongside these experts to ensure projects remain academically rigorous and policy relevant. Areas of Research Projects typically focus on governance challenges surrounding frontier AI systems. Examples include: AI incident monitoring AI governance frameworks AI safety cases International AI policy Frontier AI regulation AI risk management Open-source intelligence for AI governance Dangerous capability thresholds AI accountability mechanisms Loss-of-control scenarios International governance infrastructure Research themes evolve with emerging developments in AI governance. Outstanding Career Outcomes for Alumni One of the strongest features of the AI Governance Taskforce is its exceptional alumni network. Graduates have progressed into positions at organizations including: Google DeepMind SaferAI ControlAI Pour Demain Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative MIT AI Risk Initiative Centre for Long-Term Resilience The Future Society GovAI IAPS Future Impact Group Many alumni have also: Secured research management positions Joined international AI governance fellowships Collaborated with renowned AI researcher Yoshua Bengio Started independent AI governance initiatives Returned to the Taskforce as Research Team Leaders These achievements demonstrate the programme s effectiveness as a launchpad for careers in frontier AI governance. International Recognition of Research Research produced through the Taskforce has received significant international recognition. Achievements include: Acceptance at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) Technical AI Governance Workshop Best Paper Award recognition Co-authorship opportunities with expert partners Features in Time Magazine Coverage in the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists Publication in the AI Policy Bulletin These accomplishments reflect the quality and impact of the programme s research outputs. Who Should Apply? Arcadia Impact is seeking motivated professionals who have already begun transitioning toward careers in frontier AI governance. Applicants should demonstrate genuine commitment rather than simply exploring the field. Professionals from a wide variety of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including: Law Public Policy Economics Political Science International Relations Engineering Machine Learning Software Engineering Systems Engineering Mechanical Engineering Safety Engineering Computer Science Philosophy Social Sciences Humanities Management Applicants do not need to possess deep technical AI expertise. Eligibility Requirements Applicants should be able to: Commit approximately eight hours per week throughout the programme. Work effectively within a structured remote research team. Demonstrate commitment to reducing catastrophic risks from frontier AI. Show evidence of progressing toward a career in AI governance. Communicate clearly through writing and research. Exercise sound judgement when evaluating AI governance challenges. Work independently with minimal supervision. Arcadia Impact encourages applications even from candidates who meet only part of the preferred profile. What the Selection Committee Looks For Applications are assessed using several criteria, including: 1. Motivation Candidates should demonstrate a clear commitment to transitioning into frontier AI governance. 2. Awareness of the AI Landscape Applicants should understand: Frontier AI capabilities Emerging AI risks Key organizations Existing governance initiatives 3. Transferable Expertise Professional knowledge from previous careers should be applicable to AI governance research. 4. Research Skills Strong reasoning, writing, analytical thinking, and policy research skills are highly valued. 5. Independent Initiative Candidates should show evidence of creating opportunities independently and pursuing meaningful work without needing formal structures. Application Process The Autumn 2026 selection process consists of four stages. Stage One – General Application Applicants submit: Curriculum Vitae (CV) Short written responses No writing sample is required. Stage Two – Project Application Shortlisted candidates receive: Project briefs A short written task related to their preferred project Stage Three – Interview Successful applicants participate in an online interview where they discuss: Motivation Experience Research interests Career goals Stage Four – Offers Selected candidates receive offers to join a specific research team. Approximately 20 Research Associate positions will be available. Important Dates Applicants should carefully note the following timeline: Activity Date Applications Open 5 August 2026 General Application Deadline 31 August 2026 (Anywhere on Earth) Stage Two Invitations By 7 September 2026 Project Applications Due 13 September 2026 Interview Invitations 21 September 2026 Interviews Late September 2026 Offers Issued Week commencing 5 October 2026 Programme Begins 12 October 2026 Programme Ends 15 January 2027 Why You Should Apply Although the programme is unpaid, participants receive benefits that can significantly accelerate careers in AI governance. These include: Working directly with internationally recognized AI governance experts Building a strong professional network Producing publishable policy research Strengthening research credentials Gaining exposure to real-world AI governance challenges Improving opportunities for future fellowships and employment Collaborating with professionals from multiple disciplines Contributing to research that influences AI policy discussions worldwide For professionals committed to shaping the future of AI governance, this represents an exceptional learning and career development opportunity. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit their application through the official Arcadia Impact application portal before the deadline. Applicants with questions about the programme may contact: Ben R Smith Taskforce Lead Email: ben [at] arcadiaimpact [dot] org APPLY HERE Application Deadline Applications close at 23:59 Anywhere on Earth (AoE) on Monday, 31 August 2026 (12:59 BST on Tuesday, 1 September 2026). Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications well before the deadline due to the competitive selection process. Visit HERE to learn more about the Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026. Conclusion The Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026 Cohort offers an outstanding opportunity for experienced professionals who want to transition into one of the world s most important emerging fields. Through expert mentorship, collaborative research, international networking, and hands-on policy development, participants gain the experience and credibility needed to contribute meaningfully to frontier AI governance. Whether your background is in law, engineering, public policy, economics, philosophy, political science, or another discipline, this programme provides a structured pathway into AI governance while allowing you to continue your current professional commitments. Given the programme s strong alumni outcomes and international recognition, professionals interested in shaping the future governance of transformative AI should strongly consider applying. title: Free Net Zero Learning Pathway by UN SDG:Learn | Learn Climate Action and Science-Based Targets
summary: Are you interested in climate action, sustainability, and achieving a net-zero future? The UN SDG:Learn Net Zero Learning Pathway offers a free opportunity for learners worldwide to develop a comprehensive understanding of net-zero emissions, climate science, and science-based targets. Developed through collaboration with leading United Nations partners, this self-paced learning pathway helps individuals, professionals, students, policymakers, and organizations understand how to align climate actions with global goals and contribute to a more sustainable future. The pathway combines three specialized courses that guide learners from foundational concepts to practical implementation of net-zero strategies. About the Net Zero Learning Pathway The Net Zero Learning Pathway introduces participants to the science behind climate change, the importance of achieving net-zero emissions, and the frameworks used by organizations worldwide to set and achieve climate goals. Through a structured learning journey, participants will: • Understand the fundamentals of net-zero emissions. • Learn why climate action is critical for sustainable development. • Explore practical approaches to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. • Understand science-based target methodologies. • Learn how organizations align climate commitments with the 1.5°C pathway. • Gain knowledge of internationally recognized net-zero standards. The pathway is completely online and self-paced, allowing learners to study at their convenience. What You Will Learn The learning pathway is divided into three modules that progressively build climate knowledge and practical skills. Module 1 : Understanding Net Zero Course 1 : The Net-Zero Standard Provider : United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) This course introduces learners to the concept of net-zero emissions and explains why reaching net zero is essential for addressing climate change. Participants will explore: • Climate science fundamentals. • The role of net-zero strategies in limiting global warming. • Key concepts and terminology related to net-zero commitments. • Practical actions that organizations and individuals can take to reduce emissions. This course provides the foundation needed to understand broader climate action frameworks. Module 2 : Science-Based Targets for Net Zero Course 2 : Net Zero 101: What, Why and How Provider :United Nations University (UNU) This introductory course examines the importance of net-zero commitments and provides practical guidance on how organizations can contribute to global climate goals. Participants will learn: • What net zero means in practice. • Why net-zero commitments matter. • How emissions reductions contribute to climate mitigation. • Key approaches for implementing climate strategies. • The relationship between sustainability and long-term resilience. The course is ideal for individuals seeking a broader understanding of climate solutions and net-zero implementation. Module 3: The Net-Zero Standard in Practice Course 3 : Setting Science-Based Targets to Achieve Net-Zero Provider : United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) This advanced course focuses on helping organizations establish science-based targets that align with global climate objectives. Participants will explore: • Science-based target methodologies. • Setting near-term and long-term emissions reduction goals. • Aligning organizational targets with the 1.5°C climate pathway. • Best practices for implementing the Net-Zero Standard. • Strategies for measuring and tracking climate progress. This course is particularly valuable for sustainability professionals, business leaders, policymakers, and organizations seeking to strengthen their climate commitments. Who Should Enroll? The Net Zero Learning Pathway is suitable for: • Students and young professionals. • Climate and sustainability advocates. • Environmental practitioners. • Corporate sustainability teams. • Government officials and policymakers. • NGO professionals. • Researchers and academics. • Anyone interested in climate action and sustainable development. No prior experience is required to begin the pathway. Benefits of the Learning Pathway Participants will benefit from: • Free access to high-quality United Nations learning resources. • Flexible self-paced learning. • Expert insights from leading global institutions. • Practical knowledge on climate action and net-zero implementation. • Skills relevant to sustainability and environmental careers. • Increased understanding of science-based climate targets. • Enhanced capacity to contribute to organizational and community climate initiatives. Why Net Zero Matters Net-zero emissions have become a central goal in global efforts to combat climate change. Governments, businesses, institutions, and communities worldwide are adopting net-zero commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming. Understanding how net-zero frameworks operate and how science-based targets are established is increasingly important for professionals working in sustainability, environmental management, policy development, and corporate responsibility. This learning pathway provides a valuable opportunity to gain these critical skills at no cost. Conclusion The UN SDG:Learn Net Zero Learning Pathway offers a comprehensive and accessible introduction to climate action, net-zero standards, and science-based targets. Through three expertly designed courses from the United Nations Global Compact and United Nations University , learners can build the knowledge and practical skills needed to support a sustainable, low-carbon future. Whether you are a student, sustainability professional, policymaker, or simply passionate about climate action, this free learning opportunity can help you better understand the pathways toward achieving global climate goals and creating meaningful environmental impact. title: DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 Applications Open: Represent Germany, Inspire Future Scholars, and Promote International Education
summary: Germany has long been recognized as one of the world s leading destinations for higher education, research, and academic innovation. Every year, thousands of international students choose German universities and research institutions because of their world-class education, cutting-edge research opportunities, affordable study options, and vibrant multicultural environment. To encourage more students to explore these opportunities, the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) has officially opened applications for the DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 Programme . This unique initiative is designed for enthusiastic alumni and current students who have studied or conducted research in Germany and are passionate about sharing their experiences with others. The programme offers participants an opportunity to become official representatives of German higher education in their home countries by promoting study and research opportunities through presentations, outreach activities, educational events, and student engagement initiatives. If your time in Germany transformed your academic or professional journey and you are eager to motivate others to pursue similar opportunities, this programme provides the perfect platform to make an impact. What is the DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme? The DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme is an outreach initiative organized by the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD). The programme brings together former and current international students and researchers who have firsthand experience studying in Germany. Rather than serving as a traditional scholarship, the programme focuses on educational outreach and peer-to-peer engagement. Selected ambassadors use their personal experiences to educate prospective students about studying and conducting research in Germany. Young Ambassadors become trusted voices who can answer questions, share practical insights, and encourage talented students to consider Germany as a destination for higher education. Through presentations, educational fairs, seminars, university events, and other awareness activities, ambassadors help bridge the information gap between prospective applicants and German institutions. Why Germany? Germany continues to rank among the world s most attractive study destinations due to numerous academic and professional advantages. Some of these include: Internationally recognized universities High-quality education Strong research infrastructure Numerous English-taught programmes Affordable or tuition-free education at many public universities Excellent career opportunities Strong links between academia and industry Rich cultural diversity Global networking opportunities The Young Ambassadors Programme helps communicate these benefits through individuals who have personally experienced studying or researching in Germany. Purpose of the DAAD Young Ambassadors Programme The programme aims to: Promote Germany as a preferred destination for higher education. Increase awareness of German universities and research institutions. Encourage talented students to pursue international education. Share authentic experiences from former and current students. Strengthen educational cooperation between Germany and participating countries. Build a network of motivated education ambassadors. Inspire future applicants through peer engagement. What Will DAAD Young Ambassadors Do? Selected ambassadors will actively participate in promoting educational opportunities in Germany. Typical responsibilities include: 1. Sharing Personal Experiences Participants explain: Their academic journey Student life in Germany Research experiences Cultural experiences Career development after studying in Germany These firsthand stories help prospective students better understand what studying in Germany is truly like. 2. Conducting Presentations Young Ambassadors organize or participate in presentations at: Universities Colleges Schools Career fairs Education expos Information sessions These presentations introduce students to: German universities Study programmes Scholarships Research opportunities Student life Application processes 3. Participating in Educational Events Ambassadors represent DAAD during various outreach events, including: Study abroad fairs Information seminars Educational exhibitions University outreach programmes Student networking sessions 4. Inspiring Future Students A key objective is encouraging talented students to pursue academic opportunities in Germany by providing reliable information and practical advice. Who Can Apply? DAAD welcomes applications from motivated individuals who meet all eligibility requirements. Applicants must: Be nationals of India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, or Sri Lanka. Have studied or currently be studying or conducting research at a German institution. Be below 32 years of age as of 1 January 2027 . Be enthusiastic about promoting Germany through educational presentations or events. Be willing and able to participate in the online Young Ambassadors Training Workshop scheduled for November 2026 . Meeting all eligibility criteria is essential for consideration. Age Requirement Applicants must be: Under 32 years of age as of 1 January 2027 . This age requirement ensures the programme engages young professionals and recent academic participants who can effectively connect with prospective students. Previous German Study or Research Experience Applicants must have direct academic or research experience in Germany. Eligible individuals include those who: Previously studied at a German university. Are currently studying in Germany. Previously conducted research in Germany. Are currently conducting research at a German institution. Having firsthand experience enables ambassadors to provide authentic guidance to prospective applicants. Passion for Educational Outreach Academic qualifications alone are not sufficient. DAAD is looking for individuals who are: Passionate about Germany Excellent communicators Motivated to inspire others Comfortable speaking publicly Interested in educational outreach Willing to organize presentations and events Communication skills and enthusiasm play an important role in becoming an effective ambassador. Mandatory Training Workshop Successful applicants must participate in the online Young Ambassadors Training Workshop scheduled for November 2026 . The training prepares ambassadors by providing guidance on: Programme objectives Outreach strategies Presentation techniques Communication skills Promotional activities Representing DAAD professionally Attendance is mandatory. Benefits of Becoming a DAAD Young Ambassador Although this is not a scholarship programme, selected ambassadors receive valuable professional and personal development opportunities. These include: Leadership Development Participants strengthen their leadership abilities through educational outreach and public engagement. Public Speaking Experience Ambassadors gain confidence by delivering presentations and interacting with diverse audiences. Networking Opportunities Participants become part of a growing network of: DAAD representatives German institutions Education professionals Fellow ambassadors Students International Exposure The programme strengthens participants international profile while maintaining connections with Germany s academic community. Professional Recognition Serving as a DAAD Young Ambassador demonstrates commitment to international education and community engagement, enhancing professional credentials. Opportunity to Inspire Others Perhaps the greatest reward is helping future students access life-changing educational opportunities in Germany. Why Your Experience Matters Students often trust advice from peers who have already experienced studying abroad. By sharing practical experiences about: Student life Academic expectations Cultural adjustment Living costs Research opportunities Campus experiences Career development Young Ambassadors help prospective applicants make informed decisions and prepare for successful study experiences in Germany. Application Deadline Interested applicants must submit their applications before: Deadline: 30 September 2026 Late applications may not be considered, so prospective ambassadors are encouraged to apply well before the closing date. How to Apply Eligible applicants should complete the official online application through the DAAD application portal before the deadline. Applicants are encouraged to carefully review all eligibility requirements and prepare any necessary supporting information before submitting their applications. APPLY HERE Why You Should Apply If your academic journey in Germany has positively influenced your education, career, or personal growth, becoming a DAAD Young Ambassador offers an opportunity to give back. By joining this programme, you can: Inspire future generations of students. Promote international education. Share valuable academic experiences. Develop leadership and communication skills. Expand your professional network. Continue contributing to Germany s global academic community. For motivated young professionals and students who enjoy mentoring others, this programme represents an excellent opportunity to make a lasting educational impact. Visit HERE for more information about the DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 programme. Conclusion The DAAD Young Ambassadors 2027 Programme provides a meaningful opportunity for former and current students and researchers with German academic experience to become advocates for international education. Through presentations, outreach activities, and educational events, ambassadors play an important role in encouraging talented students to explore Germany s outstanding universities and research institutions. Beyond promoting study opportunities, the programme also helps participants strengthen their leadership, communication, and networking skills while remaining connected to the German academic community. If you meet the eligibility criteria and are passionate about sharing your educational journey, this is an excellent opportunity to inspire future scholars and contribute to international academic cooperation. Remember to submit your application before the 30 September 2026 deadline to be considered for the 2027 cohort. For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE. title: Chief Programs & Partnerships Officer at Women for Women International (WfWI): Global Executive Leadership Opportunity Across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and the United States
summary: Women for Women International (WfWI) is inviting experienced global development leaders to apply for the position of Chief Programs Partnerships Officer (CPPO) . This permanent executive leadership role offers an exceptional opportunity to shape the future of one of the world s leading organizations dedicated to supporting women survivors of war and conflict. The successful candidate will join WfWI s Executive Leadership Team and play a central role in defining the organization s global program strategy, strengthening institutional partnerships, ensuring program quality, guiding evidence-based decision-making, and leading global business development initiatives. The position is available to professionals who already possess the legal right to work in one of the approved countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Nigeria, Iraq, Germany, the United Kingdom, or the United States. This role is ideal for highly accomplished international development professionals with extensive experience leading complex humanitarian and development programs across multiple countries, particularly within fragile and conflict-affected settings. About Women for Women International Women for Women International (WfWI) is a globally recognized nonprofit organization committed to empowering women who have survived war, armed conflict, and humanitarian crises. Since its founding in 1993, the organization has supported more than 550,000 women across 17 conflict-affected countries , helping them rebuild their lives through economic empowerment, education, rights awareness, health information, and community leadership. WfWI currently works in countries including: Afghanistan Bosnia and Herzegovina Democratic Republic of the Congo Iraq Kosovo Nigeria Rwanda South Sudan Through its flagship Stronger Women, Stronger Nations Programme , participants gain: Livelihood and vocational skills Financial literacy Savings and income-generation knowledge Leadership development Women s rights education Health awareness Community support networks The organization believes that empowering women creates stronger families, stronger communities, and ultimately more peaceful societies. Position Overview Position: Chief Programs Partnerships Officer (CPPO) Department: Global Programs Unit Employment Type: Full-time Contract: Permanent / Open-ended Leadership Grade: L Reports To: International Chief Executive Officer Work Arrangement: Remote or Hybrid (depending on location) Eligible Work Locations Applicants must already have legal authorization to work in one of the following countries: Ghana Kenya Rwanda South Africa Nigeria Iraq Germany United Kingdom United States Women for Women International does not sponsor work visas and does not provide relocation support . An Executive Leadership Role with Global Impact The Chief Programs Partnerships Officer serves as one of the most senior executives within Women for Women International. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the CPPO helps shape the organization s future by ensuring that every program remains: Mission-driven Evidence-based Financially sustainable Operationally feasible Centered on women s needs Responsive to changing humanitarian contexts The role serves as the International CEO s principal strategic advisor on matters involving: Global program strategy Organizational growth Geographic expansion Institutional partnerships Program coherence Funding alignment Delivery continuity Rather than directly managing all country offices permanently, the CPPO provides strategic oversight through a matrix leadership structure that ensures consistent program quality across regions. Major Responsibilities The position covers several broad leadership functions. 1. Lead Global Program Strategy The CPPO will oversee the organization s entire global programming approach. Responsibilities include: Leading the development of WfWI s global program strategy Ensuring all programs remain evidence-informed Improving program quality worldwide Designing innovative interventions Maintaining global technical standards Establishing quality assurance systems Aligning all programming with organizational strategy The successful candidate will ensure that every country program delivers meaningful impact while remaining operationally realistic. 2. Strengthen Program Quality Across Regions One of the primary responsibilities is ensuring consistency throughout WfWI s international operations. This includes: Working closely with Regional Directors Supporting Country Directors Monitoring delivery quality Reviewing annual country plans Assessing implementation risks Supporting organizational transitions Maintaining strong technical oversight The CPPO will ensure that local implementation aligns with global organizational standards. 3. Guide Program Design and Innovation The executive will oversee technical teams responsible for: Program Design Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) Country Office Support Grant Management Program Planning Key duties include: Approving new program models Reviewing innovations Supporting research initiatives Strengthening evidence generation Promoting data-driven decision-making Improving operational efficiency Ensuring scalability of interventions 4. Lead the Crisis Response Fund The CPPO serves as Executive Sponsor of WfWI s Crisis Response Fund. Key responsibilities include: Chairing the Steering Committee Approving funding allocations Reviewing high-risk partnerships Supporting emergency interventions Managing conflict-response strategies Ensuring safeguarding compliance Coordinating fundraising for crisis programming This work enables WfWI to support women in countries where it may not yet maintain permanent offices. 5. Oversee Business Development An important part of the role involves leading institutional fundraising and strategic partnerships. Responsibilities include: Guiding the Global Business Development Unit Developing fundraising strategies Reviewing institutional proposals Managing donor relationships Evaluating funding opportunities Approving major grants Ensuring funding aligns with organizational priorities The CPPO has final authority over significant programmatic funding decisions. 6. Build Strategic Global Partnerships The successful executive will represent WfWI internationally. Potential partners include: Governments Bilateral agencies Multilateral organizations Universities Research institutions Think tanks International NGOs Philanthropic organizations Strategic networks The CPPO will strengthen partnerships that enhance both organizational impact and long-term sustainability. 7. Organizational Leadership As a senior executive, the CPPO will: Lead high-performing international teams Supervise senior global managers Manage large budgets Present to Executive Leadership Engage with Board committees Support organizational transformation Clarify governance structures Strengthen cross-functional collaboration Leadership Responsibilities The CPPO directly supervises: Deputy Chief Programs Partnerships Officer Global Director of Business Development Crisis Response Fund Manager Global Programs Unit Coordinator During organizational transition periods, designated Country Directors may also report directly to the CPPO. Collaboration Across the Organization The role requires close collaboration with multiple senior leaders. These include: Chief Executive Officer Supporting strategic organizational decisions and global growth. Chief Operating Officer Coordinating: Operations Procurement Finance Compliance Risk Management Security Human Resources Information Technology Chief Research, Policy, Advocacy Strategic Communications Officer Working together to ensure that: Communications reflect evidence Advocacy is informed by field realities Research influences programming Organizational messaging remains credible Required Qualifications Applicants should possess: A Master s degree in International Development, Social Sciences, Gender Studies, Humanitarian Studies, Public Policy, or a closely related discipline. At least 15 years of senior leadership experience in international development, humanitarian action, or nonprofit management. Extensive experience managing complex international program portfolios. Proven leadership in fragile and conflict-affected environments. Strong expertise in program strategy and organizational transformation. Significant experience in institutional fundraising and donor engagement. Experience managing geographically dispersed international teams. Strong strategic planning capabilities. Excellent stakeholder management skills. Deep understanding of gender equality and women s rights. Ability to work effectively within complex matrix organizations. Existing legal authorization to work in one of the listed countries. Preferred Qualifications Women for Women International would particularly value candidates who have: International leadership experience across multiple regions. Experience working in Africa and the Middle East. Strong donor and institutional networks. Experience leading research and evaluation initiatives. Knowledge of localization approaches. Experience with integrated multi-sector programming. Expertise in partnership-driven development models. Skills That Will Make Candidates Competitive Ideal applicants should demonstrate: Executive leadership Strategic vision Change management Program management Business development Partnership building Team leadership Financial oversight Communication Decision-making Negotiation Evidence-based planning Cross-cultural leadership Risk management Innovation management Benefits Women for Women International offers a competitive employment package that includes: Competitive location-adjusted salary Permanent employment Remote or hybrid work options depending on location Additional location-specific benefits Opportunity to lead global humanitarian programming Executive-level leadership experience International collaboration Significant influence on global women s empowerment initiatives Organizational Values Employees are expected to uphold WfWI s core values: Empowerment Integrity Respect Resilience Leadership principles include: Decisive Accountable Courageous Adaptable Inclusive All staff must comply with the organization s Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policies. Diversity and Inclusion Women for Women International is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where diversity is respected and celebrated. Applications are welcomed regardless of: Age Disability Gender identity Race Religion Sexual orientation Marital status Political opinion Pregnancy or maternity status The organization believes that diverse teams strengthen innovation, collaboration, and organizational performance. How to Apply Interested applicants should submit their application through the official Women for Women International careers portal. title: MSD UK 2026 Grants Programme: Apply for Funding to Tackle Health Inequalities and Improve Patient Outcomes Across the UK
summary: Healthcare organisations and patient advocacy groups across the United Kingdom now have an opportunity to secure funding through the MSD UK 2026 Grants Programme . Following the success of its 2025 programme, MSD UK has officially opened the second application window for its 2026 grants, inviting eligible organisations to submit innovative projects that address health inequalities and improve patient and population health. The programme reflects MSD UK s ongoing commitment to supporting healthcare initiatives that create meaningful, measurable, and sustainable improvements in public health. By providing arm s-length financial grants, MSD UK enables organisations to develop and implement projects that may otherwise struggle to secure funding. If your organisation is working to improve healthcare access, reduce inequalities, strengthen community care, promote disease prevention, or leverage digital innovation for healthier communities, this funding opportunity could help bring your project to life. About the MSD UK Grants Programme The MSD UK Grants Programme is designed to provide financial support to eligible healthcare and patient organisations that are committed to improving health outcomes throughout the United Kingdom. Rather than funding routine operations, the programme focuses on supporting projects that have the potential to create lasting positive change by addressing some of the UK s most pressing healthcare challenges. The programme specifically seeks initiatives that: Reduce health inequalities. Improve patient experiences and outcomes. Support healthier populations. Strengthen healthcare delivery. Encourage innovation in healthcare services. Promote sustainable public health improvements. MSD UK believes that many impactful healthcare projects never move beyond the planning stage due to financial constraints. Through this grants programme, the organisation aims to help remove that barrier and enable meaningful community impact. Building on the Success of the 2025 Programme The 2025 MSD UK Grants Programme received an unprecedented number of applications, demonstrating the growing need for funding within the healthcare sector. Highlights from the previous programme include: Two application windows. A record number of submissions. Funding awarded to 18 impactful healthcare projects. Support provided to organisations working directly with patients and local communities. Following this success, MSD UK has expanded its commitment by launching another funding round for 2026. Focus Areas for the 2026 Grants Programme The 2026 programme places particular emphasis on projects that respond to evolving priorities within the UK healthcare system. Eligible projects should address one or more of the following themes: 1. Community and Neighbourhood Care MSD UK is interested in initiatives that strengthen healthcare delivery within local communities. Examples include: Community healthcare services Local health partnerships Neighbourhood-based patient support Integrated care approaches Community outreach programmes Projects should demonstrate how they improve healthcare accessibility and patient experiences at the local level. 2. Who Can Apply? Applications are open to eligible healthcare organisations and patient organisations operating within the United Kingdom . These organisations should have projects that align with MSD UK s objectives of improving patient care, reducing health inequalities, and supporting public health priorities. Many innovative organisations have ideas capable of transforming patient care but lack sufficient financial resources to implement them. The MSD UK Grants Programme seeks to bridge this gap by supporting projects that: Improve access to healthcare. Reduce disparities in health outcomes. Strengthen local healthcare systems. Empower patients. Promote healthier lifestyles. Encourage innovation within healthcare delivery. title: Spark Microgrants in Malawi: How Inclusive Village Planning is Empowering Communities Through Local Leadership and Direct Village Grants
summary: Across many rural communities in Africa, sustainable development is most effective when local people are empowered to make decisions about their own future. Rather than relying solely on externally designed development programs, communities often possess the knowledge, leadership, experience, and innovative ideas needed to solve their own challenges. Spark Microgrants is championing this approach in Malawi by supporting community-led development that places decision-making directly into the hands of local residents. Through inclusive village planning, direct village grants, leadership development, and collaboration with community-based organizations, the initiative is helping communities identify their own priorities and transform those priorities into lasting development outcomes. The initiative is currently expanding its work across Kasungu and Zomba districts in Malawi, where it aims to reach approximately 33,000 people in 100 villages. The lessons learned from this work are also expected to contribute to broader government-led efforts to strengthen local development planning across the country. About Spark Microgrants Spark Microgrants is an organization dedicated to enabling communities to drive their own development through locally led decision-making and investment. Instead of imposing development priorities from outside, Spark Microgrants believes that communities themselves are best positioned to identify their most urgent needs and design practical solutions. Its model focuses on: Inclusive village planning Community leadership development Direct financial support through village grants Strengthening local governance Building long-term community ownership Encouraging participation from marginalized groups The organization works alongside local partners to ensure development initiatives are community-owned, transparent, and sustainable. Supporting Community-Led Development in Rural Malawi The current initiative focuses on rural communities throughout Malawi where local residents are encouraged to become the primary architects of their own development. Instead of outside organizations determining community priorities, residents participate in structured planning processes that allow them to: Discuss local challenges Identify development priorities Build consensus Create practical village development plans Manage project implementation Oversee financial resources This participatory approach ensures that projects reflect genuine community needs rather than externally determined objectives. Inclusive Village Planning at the Centre of Development One of the defining features of Spark Microgrants is its emphasis on inclusive village planning. Communities participate in structured planning sessions where everyone has the opportunity to contribute ideas regarding local development priorities. The planning process encourages communities to think collectively about improving: Livelihoods Infrastructure Community services Local economic opportunities Social wellbeing Community resilience Rather than relying on a small group of local leaders, the planning process actively encourages broad participation from across the community. Empowering Women, Youth and Marginalized Groups An important component of the initiative is ensuring that development planning represents the voices of all community members. Spark Microgrants intentionally promotes participation from groups that have historically been excluded from local decision-making processes. These include: Women Young people Individuals traditionally excluded from leadership roles Underrepresented community members By broadening participation, communities are able to produce more inclusive development plans that reflect shared aspirations rather than the priorities of only a few individuals. The organization also trains elected community facilitators, with half of these facilitators being women. These facilitators guide village planning discussions, encourage participation, and help communities move from planning to implementation. Direct Village Grants for Community Priorities After communities identify their priorities and prepare development plans, Spark Microgrants provides direct village grants that allow communities to implement their own projects. Instead of outside agencies managing every aspect of implementation, residents themselves oversee the use of resources. Community members are responsible for: Managing project funds. Coordinating implementation. Monitoring progress. Ensuring accountability. Maintaining completed projects. This community ownership strengthens local accountability while building long-term leadership capacity. Partnership with Community-Based Organizations Spark Microgrants works closely with Malawian community-based organizations that understand local contexts and community needs. These partnerships help ensure that: Community engagement remains culturally appropriate. Local knowledge informs implementation. Capacity is strengthened within existing organizations. Development efforts remain sustainable. Working through local organizations also helps strengthen community institutions that will continue supporting development beyond the duration of individual projects. Expansion Across Kasungu and Zomba The initiative will be implemented in: Kasungu District Zomba District Across these districts, Spark Microgrants plans to support: 100 villages Approximately 33,000 people This represents a significant expansion of community-led development efforts designed to improve local governance and strengthen community participation. Building Evidence for National Scale An important objective of the initiative is not only to support current communities but also to generate evidence for future policy development. The experience gained from implementation across the participating villages will inform an anticipated next phase involving collaboration with: The Government of Malawi The World Bank The future phase is expected to explore how inclusive village planning can be integrated into district government systems, giving communities a stronger voice in shaping local development priorities. If successful, the model could influence how community participation is incorporated into public planning processes throughout Malawi. Community Savings and Collective Investment Beyond planning and grants, participating communities also establish communal savings mechanisms. These savings are collectively managed by the village and provide opportunities for communities to: Build financial resilience. Invest in shared priorities. Support future development activities. Strengthen local ownership of community assets. Collective financial management reinforces accountability while creating long-term community investment structures. Key Features of the Spark Microgrants Model Some of the major components of the initiative include: Community-led decision-making Inclusive village planning Direct village grants Leadership development Women s participation in leadership Youth engagement Partnership with local organizations Community-managed investments Collective savings initiatives Strengthened local governance Evidence generation for national policy Collaboration with government institutions Why This Initiative Matters Traditional development models often rely heavily on external planning and implementation. Spark Microgrants demonstrates an alternative approach where communities: Identify their own priorities. Design their own solutions. Manage their own resources. Strengthen local leadership. Build long-term ownership. By placing decision-making in the hands of local residents, the initiative supports sustainable development that reflects the unique needs and aspirations of each community. Its emphasis on inclusion, accountability, and local ownership also contributes to stronger governance systems and greater community resilience. APPLY HERE Learn More Individuals interested in learning more about Spark Microgrants and its work can visit the organization s official website for additional information about its community-led development approach and global initiatives. Visit HERE for more information about the Spark Microgrants in Malawi. Conclusion Spark Microgrants is helping reshape rural development in Malawi by demonstrating that communities are capable of leading their own progress when provided with the necessary tools, resources, and support. Through inclusive planning, direct village grants, leadership development, and partnerships with local organizations, the initiative empowers residents to determine their own future while strengthening local governance and community ownership. With implementation across 100 villages in Kasungu and Zomba expected to benefit approximately 33,000 people, the initiative also serves as an important learning opportunity for future collaboration with the Government of Malawi and the World Bank. If successfully integrated into district planning systems, this community-led approach has the potential to influence development practices far beyond the initial project areas, creating stronger and more inclusive pathways for local development across Malawi. title: Imagine Award Grant – $20,000 Funding for Early Childhood Changemakers in the U.S.
summary: Introduction The Imagine Award by the Promise Fund stands as one of the most transformative opportunities for early childhood innovators across the United States. Designed to empower community-rooted leaders , this award provides $20,000 in flexible funding and a six-month cohort-based learning experience to help changemakers turn their ideas into reality. Since 2018, the Promise Venture Studio has been committed to equipping social innovators with the resources, relationships, and runway they need to build a more abundant and just future for young children and families. The Imagine Award continues this legacy by focusing on leaders who are deeply connected to their communities and who bring firsthand insight into the challenges faced by families. This award is not just about financial support—it is about building capacity, fostering innovation, and strengthening leadership . Recipients will learn how to design and execute lightweight tests for rapid learning, gain clarity on their idea’s direction using impact and business models, and craft compelling stories to attract future partnerships. The Imagine Award is a call to action for those who believe in equity, justice, and community-driven change . It invites leaders who are ready to pilot transformative ideas that can reshape early childhood experiences, ensuring that every child has access to opportunity, care, and growth. What the Imagine Award Provides $20,000 Flexible Grant Funding Funds can be used at the recipient’s discretion to pursue tests or pilots of transformative ideas. Flexibility ensures leaders can adapt resources to their unique contexts. Partnership with Promise Direct, one-on-one support from the Promise team. Tailored help and relevant connections to strengthen pilots. In-Person Convening Multi-day gatherings for peer connection, learning, and pilot design. Mentoring Access to experienced mentors to guide awardees through pilot design and beyond. Cohort Workshops and Gatherings Light, tailored coaching to support pilot preparation, launch, and implementation. Alumni Support Ongoing peer community and resources for continued learning and collaboration. Who the Imagine Award Funds Awardees are expected to be: Based in and primarily serving children and families in the U.S. Deeply connected to communities impacted by their work. Self-motivated, creative problem solvers with a bent toward action. Committed to working alongside communities and centering community voice. Equipped with expertise and capacity to pursue the work. Prepared to execute a pilot within six months of receiving the award. Ideas funded should be: Clearly defined. In or ready to enter a phase of initial testing/piloting. In need of resources to move forward. Driven by a strong commitment to equity and justice. Application Timeline July 7, 2026: Applications open July August 2026: Pilot workshops and Q A sessions offered August 28, 2026: Applications close Early October 2026: Finalist interviews November 6, 2026: Awards announced January 2027: Award programming begins July 2027: Award programming ends Apply HERE today! Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. What is the Imagine Award? The Imagine Award is a funding and learning opportunity offered by the Promise Fund to support early childhood leaders at the idea stage. It provides $20,000 in flexible funding and a six-month cohort program to help recipients pilot their ideas and refine their approaches. 2. Who is eligible to apply? Applicants must be based in and primarily serving children and families in the United States . They should be deeply connected to their communities and ready to execute a pilot within six months of receiving the award. 3. What does “community-rooted leader” mean? A community-rooted leader is someone who has firsthand experience and deep connections with the communities they serve. This ensures that their solutions are grounded in real needs and lived experiences. 4. What is meant by “flexible funding”? Flexible funding means that recipients can use the $20,000 grant at their discretion to pursue tests or pilots of their transformative ideas. There are no rigid restrictions on how the funds must be spent. 5. What stage should my idea be in? Your idea should be clearly defined and ready to enter a phase of initial testing or piloting. The Imagine Award supports innovators at the idea stage , helping them move from concept to implementation. 6. How long does the program last? The program runs for six months , beginning in January 2027 and ending in July 2027 . 7. What kind of support will I receive? Awardees receive one-on-one mentorship, tailored coaching, peer learning opportunities, and access to a network of experts and alumni. 8. What is the application timeline? July 7, 2026: Applications open July August 2026: Pilot workshops and Q A sessions offered August 28, 2026: Applications close Early October 2026: Finalist interviews November 6, 2026: Awards announced January 2027: Award programming begins July 2027: Award programming ends 9. How many awards are available? The number of awards varies each year, but multiple leaders are selected to form a cohort. 10. What happens after the program ends? Awardees join the Promise Fund alumni community , gaining ongoing access to peer support, resources, and collaboration opportunities. 11. Can international applicants apply? No. The Imagine Award is open only to leaders based in and serving communities within the United States . 12. What kind of ideas are funded? Ideas should be clearly defined, equity-driven, and ready for initial testing. They must aim to create transformative impact in early childhood development. 13. What is the time commitment required? Awardees should be prepared to dedicate consistent time to their pilot and cohort activities throughout the six-month program. 14. How are milestones set during the program? Promise works collaboratively with awardees to set tailored milestones that align with their project goals and community needs. 15. What kind of mentorship is provided? Awardees have access to a bench of mentors who guide them through pilot design, implementation, and post-program transitions. 16. How does Promise ensure equity and inclusion? Promise prioritizes leaders and ideas that center community voice, equity, and justice. The program actively seeks diversity in its cohorts. 17. What is the Promise Fund? The Promise Fund is an initiative by Promise Venture Studio that supports social innovators in early childhood through funding, mentorship, and community-building. 18. What is the selection process like? Applications are reviewed by a committee that evaluates clarity of ideas, community connection, readiness for piloting, and commitment to equity. Finalists are interviewed before the final selection. 19. What happens if my idea changes during the program? Flexibility is encouraged. Awardees can refine and adapt their ideas based on feedback and learning throughout the program. 20. How does Promise highlight awardees’ work? Promise amplifies awardees’ stories through its platforms, showcasing their impact and leadership in the early childhood innovation space. 21. Can previous applicants reapply? Yes, previous applicants can reapply if they meet the eligibility criteria. 22. What is the long-term impact of the Imagine Award? The award helps leaders build sustainable models for their ideas, fostering long-term change in early childhood systems and communities. To lean more about the Imagine Award Grant, click HERE. Conclusion The Imagine Award by the Promise Fund is more than a grant—it is a movement to empower community-rooted leaders who are shaping the future of early childhood development. With $20,000 in flexible funding , mentorship, and a six-month learning journey, awardees gain the tools, confidence, and connections needed to transform their ideas into impactful pilots. This award recognizes that innovation begins at the community level. By supporting leaders who understand the lived experiences of families and children, the Promise Fund ensures that solutions are equitable, sustainable, and deeply relevant. For those ready to take the next step in their journey as changemakers, the Imagine Award offers an unparalleled opportunity to learn, grow, and lead. title: Scaleup Europe Fund 2026: Europe’s €5 Billion Growth Fund for High-Potential Deep Tech Companies
summary: The Scaleup Europe Fund (SEF) is a landmark multi-billion-euro investment initiative created to accelerate the growth of Europe s most promising technology companies. Designed to strengthen Europe s competitiveness in strategic industries, the Fund will provide substantial late-stage and growth capital to innovative businesses developing breakthrough technologies across the continent. Backed by the European Commission and some of Europe s largest institutional investors, the Scaleup Europe Fund aims to bridge the investment gap facing European scaleups and ensure that high-growth companies have access to the financial resources they need to expand globally while remaining rooted in Europe. As part of the European Union Startup and Scaleup Strategy , the Fund represents one of the largest coordinated efforts to support strategic technology innovation, helping Europe compete with global innovation leaders while strengthening economic resilience and technological sovereignty. With its first investments expected to begin in autumn 2026 , the Scaleup Europe Fund is positioned to become one of Europe s most influential investment vehicles for deep technology companies. About the Scaleup Europe Fund The Scaleup Europe Fund is a €5 billion late-stage and growth investment fund established to support European companies operating in strategic technology sectors. Unlike traditional startup funding programmes that focus on early-stage ventures, the Scaleup Europe Fund specifically targets companies that have already demonstrated significant growth potential and are ready to scale internationally. The Fund seeks to ensure that Europe s most innovative businesses can continue expanding without relocating outside Europe in search of large-scale investment. By mobilizing both public and private capital, the Fund creates an investment platform capable of supporting ambitious companies developing technologies that are critical to Europe s future competitiveness. Why the Scaleup Europe Fund Was Created Europe has produced thousands of innovative startups over the past decade. However, many successful companies have struggled to secure the large-scale financing required for international expansion. As a result, numerous European technology companies have sought investment abroad or relocated to other regions where growth capital is more readily available. The Scaleup Europe Fund addresses this challenge by: Increasing access to late-stage investment. Supporting Europe s technology champions. Closing the funding gap between Europe and global innovation leaders. Strengthening European technological sovereignty. Keeping high-growth companies headquartered in Europe. Encouraging long-term innovation and economic growth. The initiative aligns with the European Union s broader industrial and competitiveness agenda. Purpose of the Fund The Scaleup Europe Fund has several strategic objectives: Support Europe s fastest-growing technology companies. Provide large-scale growth financing. Strengthen Europe s deep technology ecosystem. Accelerate commercialization of breakthrough innovations. Promote long-term economic competitiveness. Encourage sustainable technological leadership. Foster collaboration between public institutions and private investors. Enable European innovators to expand globally while remaining based in Europe. APPLY HERE Strategic Technology Areas The Fund focuses on companies developing technologies considered strategically important for Europe s future. Priority sectors include: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Supporting companies developing advanced AI systems, applications, infrastructure, and intelligent software solutions. Quantum Technologies Investing in innovations involving quantum computing, quantum communications, quantum sensing, and related technologies. Semiconductor Technologies Supporting companies advancing semiconductor design, manufacturing, materials, and supply chain resilience. Robotics and Autonomous Systems Funding innovations in robotics, automation, autonomous mobility, intelligent manufacturing, and industrial automation. Energy Technologies Supporting technologies that accelerate clean energy generation, storage, efficiency, and sustainable energy systems. Space Technologies Investing in companies developing satellite technologies, launch systems, Earth observation, space infrastructure, and related innovations. Biotechnology Supporting breakthrough biological innovations across healthcare, agriculture, and industrial biotechnology. Medical Technologies Funding companies developing advanced healthcare technologies, diagnostics, digital health, and medical devices. Advanced Materials Supporting innovations in next-generation materials with applications across multiple industries. Agritech Investing in technologies that improve agricultural productivity, sustainability, food systems, and climate resilience. Geographic Scope The Scaleup Europe Fund supports eligible companies located across: European Union Member States. All regions of Europe participating within the programme framework. The Fund aims to ensure broad geographic representation rather than concentrating investment in only a few innovation hubs. Public-Private Partnership One of the defining characteristics of the Scaleup Europe Fund is its strong collaboration between public institutions and private investors. The Fund combines: Public investment leadership. Private sector expertise. Institutional investment capital. Market-based investment management. This structure is intended to maximize commercial performance while supporting strategic European priorities. Founding Investors The Fund is supported by an impressive group of founding investors alongside the European Commission. These include: Novo Holdings EIFO (Export and Investment Fund of Denmark) CriteriaCaixa Santander / Mouro Capital Fondazione Compagnia San Paolo Intesa Sanpaolo Fondazione Cariplo APG Asset Management (acting on behalf of Dutch pension fund ABP) Wallenberg Investments Allianz These organizations collectively contribute significant investment expertise and financial capacity to the Fund. Relationship with the European Innovation Council (EIC) The Scaleup Europe Fund will operate: Under the existing European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund umbrella structure . However, the Fund will be managed through: A fully privately owned. Market-based fund management structure. This governance model combines the strategic vision of European institutions with professional investment management. Part of the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy The Scaleup Europe Fund is one of the flagship initiatives announced under the EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy . The initiative was introduced by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen during the 2025 State of the Union Address . Its vision is simple: Enable Europe s most innovative companies to choose Europe as the best place to build, scale, and compete globally. Fund Manager Selection Following a competitive international selection process, the European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund Board selected: EQT to serve as the preferred: Investment adviser. Fund manager. EQT was selected after a rigorous evaluation process designed to identify the most qualified organization to manage the Fund s investments. Why EQT Was Selected The selection process emphasized: Investment expertise. Experience managing large-scale growth funds. Knowledge of deep technology investments. Ability to operate independently.
